title: Structural quality gate catches table/code-block loss

brief.why: Trafilatura passes the 10% ratio check but drops critical structured content. ISO country codes page: 249-row data table stripped despite include_tables=True (trafilatura output 96% of page text but zero table data). Python docs: code blocks flattened into inline text. The ratio check measures quantity not quality — structural degradation is invisible.
brief.what: 1. After trafilatura extraction, count structural markers in the output (pipe-tables or markdown tables, fenced code blocks) 2. Compare against page DOM signals via eval: number of <table> rows with >2 cells, number of <pre> or <code> blocks with >50 chars 3. If page has significant tables/code but trafilatura output has none, fall through to Readability which preserves both better 4. Thresholds: page has >=5 table data rows and output has 0 table markers → reject. Page has >=2 long code blocks and output has 0 fenced blocks → reject 5. Add tests for both table-loss and code-loss detection 6. Smoke test against ISO country codes page and Python asyncio docs
brief.done: ISO country codes page produces output containing table data (country names and codes). Python asyncio docs produce output with fenced code blocks. Cascade falls through to Readability when trafilatura drops structure. Existing pages (Wikipedia article, ONS, HN) unaffected.

Compare against page DOM signals via eval: number of <table> rows with >2 cells, number of <pre> or <code> blocks with >50 chars
If page has significant tables/code but trafilatura output has none, fall through to Readability which preserves both better

title: capture verb records network requests during a passe script

brief.why: passe has zero use of the CDP Network domain. chrome-log is a daemon that watches all tabs. There's a gap: planned, single-tab, ephemeral network capture during a script — 'goto URL, do stuff, show me what API calls it made.' Useful for reverse-engineering SPAs without running the always-on daemon.
brief.what: 1. Add capture verb that enables Network.enable on passe's tab 2. Buffer Network.requestWillBeSent and Network.responseReceived events during the script 3. At end of script (or on explicit capture-stop), write collected requests to JSONL file 4. Include method, URL, status, headers, timing 5. Optional: capture response bodies (large — make opt-in) 6. Consider capture-start/capture-stop pair vs whole-script capture 7. Keep it ephemeral — no daemon, no multi-tab
brief.done: passe run -c 'capture /tmp/reqs.jsonl; goto https://spa.example.com; click .search; wait 2000' produces a JSONL file of all network requests made during the script. Response bodies opt-in via --bodies flag.

title: Event buffer doesn't grow unbounded in long scripts

brief.done: Event buffer has a documented bound. Long scripts don't accumulate stale events.

title: Passe doesn't lose fast navigations to a race condition

brief.why: wait-navigation registers its Page.loadEventFired listener AFTER the triggering action (click, press) has already dispatched. Fast navigations fire the event before the waiter exists, so it's dropped and wait-navigation hangs until timeout.
brief.what: 1. Add event buffering to CDPClient — store events that fire with no waiter 2. Check buffer in wait_for_event before registering a new future 3. Test: click that triggers navigation followed by wait-navigation resolves instantly
brief.done: Script 'click .nav-link; wait-navigation' resolves without timeout when the click triggers a fast navigation. Existing do_navigate (listener-before-dispatch) still works. Existing tests pass.

brief.what: 1. Add batch subcommand: passe batch <file-or-urls> --out <dir> 2. Reads URLs from a file (one per line) or accepts multiple URL args 3. Processes them using the fetch pipeline (goto + auto-wait + read) 4. Output: one markdown file per URL in the output directory, named by slug 5. Consider parallelism options: multiple tabs in same Chrome (CDP supports this), or sequential-but-fast 6. Report summary: URLs processed, succeeded, failed, total time 7. Could also accept stdin for piping from snapshot output
brief.done: echo 'https://docs.utiq.com/docs/utiq-technology\nhttps://docs.utiq.com/docs/data-activation' | passe batch --out /tmp/utiq/ reads both pages and deposits markdown files. Total time significantly less than 2x single-page time.

title: Passe warns when read extraction looks incomplete

brief.why: read reports ok:true even when Readability captures garbage (cookie banners, animated content, SPA nav chrome). No signal to the caller that extraction is incomplete — discovered through field testing against Daily Mail, entire.io, etc.
brief.what: 1. Modify EXTRACT_JS to return pageTextLength (document.body.innerText.length) alongside markdown 2. In do_read, compare extracted markdown length vs page text length — warn if <10% 3. Add warning field to step info in run_script for read verb 4. Warn on fallback extraction too
brief.done: passe run -c 'goto SPA-page; read' emits a warning in stderr NDJSON when extraction is <10% of page text. Fallback extractions also warn. Warning visible in step_info but does not set ok:false (it's a warning, not an error).

title: Agent can drive OAuth flows end-to-end via Chrome Debug

brief.why: Remote gcloud auth required 5+ tool calls, manual code extraction, pty hacks, and a stale-code bug. Any headless OAuth flow (not just gcloud) needs the same pattern: navigate visible tab → user approves → capture redirect/code. Passe should make this smooth.
brief.what: 1. Ship --keep-tab and --reuse-tab flags (passe-rosuke, passe-nononi already tracked) 2. Add wait-for-navigation verb that blocks until URL matches a pattern (e.g. wait-url-match sdk.cloud.google.com/authcode) 3. Add eval to extract content from the current page without re-navigating 4. Document the OAuth-via-passe pattern in the skill (navigate → user approves → capture code → feed back to CLI)
brief.done: A gcloud remote auth can be done in 3 passe calls: navigate to OAuth URL in visible tab, wait for redirect, extract code. No pty hacks, no polling loops, no stale-code bugs.

title: passe --help lists all verbs with one-line descriptions

brief.why: No introspectable help — the only documentation is CLAUDE.md and the skill. Every other CLI tool has a verb listing. A Claude running passe for the first time has no way to discover capabilities from the CLI itself.
brief.what: 1. Add passe run --help that lists all verbs grouped by category (Navigation, Interaction, Observation, Control) with one-line descriptions 2. Include flags (--keep-tab, --reuse-tab, --no-wait, --source) 3. Consider passe verbs as a standalone subcommand for quick reference
brief.done: passe run --help prints a categorized verb reference. passe --help shows subcommands and global flags.

title: crawl verb follows same-domain links and reads each page

brief.why: Research tasks often need to read an entire docs site. The Utiq session required discovering the nav tree via snapshot, manually extracting URLs, then visiting each one sequentially — 10 separate passe calls. A crawl verb would automate this common pattern.
brief.what: 1. Add crawl verb: crawl <url> [--depth N] [--same-domain] [--selector css] <output-dir> 2. Visits the starting URL, discovers links (optionally filtered by CSS selector for nav elements), follows them to --depth (default 1) 3. Deposits one markdown file per page in output-dir, named by URL slug 4. Respects --same-domain to avoid following external links 5. Uses the fetch pipeline internally (auto-wait + read cascade) 6. Reports summary: pages found, pages read, pages skipped, total time 7. Consider parallelising page reads (open multiple tabs? or sequential but fast with auto-wait)
brief.done: passe run -c 'crawl https://docs.utiq.com/docs/utiq-technology --depth 1 --same-domain /tmp/utiq-docs/' produces one markdown file per linked docs page. Completes in under 10 seconds for a 10-page site.

title: outerHTML includes shadow DOM content — extractors see the full page

brief.why: document.documentElement.outerHTML skips shadow root content. MDN uses <mdn-code-example> web components with code inside shadow DOM — 17 code examples (8KB) invisible to both trafilatura and Readability. Any site using web components loses content silently.
brief.what: 1. Write a JS flattener function that walks the DOM tree, finds elements with .shadowRoot, and inlines shadow root children into the light DOM before serialization 2. Replace the do_eval('document.documentElement.outerHTML') call in do_read with the flattener 3. Test against MDN Promise page — should recover all 17 code examples (8191 chars) 4. Test against regular pages (Wikipedia, ONS) — flattener must not break non-shadow-DOM pages 5. Test performance — flattening adds DOM walking overhead, measure on a heavy page
brief.done: passe run -c 'goto MDN_PROMISE_URL; read /tmp/out.md' produces markdown with fenced code blocks from shadow DOM. grep -c backtick-fence returns >0. Regular pages unaffected. No performance regression >100ms.

title: Replace Readability.js primary path with trafilatura cascade

brief.why: read only works on articles. Trafilatura handles any page type and produces better markdown with tables, code blocks, and links. Chrome gives us the rendered DOM; trafilatura cleans it server-side.
brief.what: 1. Add trafilatura to pyproject.toml dependencies 2. Refactor do_read: get outerHTML + innerText length from Chrome via eval, run trafilatura.extract with include_formatting=True on Python side 3. If trafilatura returns None or too short, fall back to current Readability.js+Turndown path 4. If Readability also fails, fall back to innerText (existing behaviour) 5. Keep ratio warning system — compare trafilatura output length vs page innerText length 6. Update tests — mock the new flow, test cascade fallback 7. Update CLAUDE.md — read is no longer articles-only 8. Reinstall and smoke test against my.itv.com
brief.done: passe run -c 'goto URL; read /tmp/out.md' uses trafilatura as primary extractor. Falls back to Readability then innerText. Tests pass. my.itv.com hub page produces clean markdown.
